note: Reference data for the topic picker and the script writer: formats, hooks and ideas that work for other Shorts channels. Learn the shape, never copy titles, scripts or footage. 'recent' is refreshed in the cloud (app/ideabank.py) from the reference channels; the rest was built from vidIQ (titles, view counts, two transcripts).

formats.name: the N parts / rules
formats.shape: Claim 'Every X is built on N parts. Here they are.' then one beat per part, end on the payoff.
formats.example: The 4 parts every viral short drama is built on (Higgsfield)

formats.name: it's not what it looks like
formats.shape: Show the impossible-looking thing, then 'here's the trick' with the real mechanism.
formats.example: Tesla's flying Roadster isn't really flying. Here's the trick (2.4M views)

formats.name: how it really works
formats.shape: Everyday or famous machine, one surprising mechanism, one number, one image of the inside.
formats.example: How submarines make their own air and fresh water (275K)

formats.name: tech news, explained
formats.shape: This week's tech headline, what it actually does, the one number that matters, why it matters to you.
formats.example: How GTA 6 reaches millions of consoles at once (315K)

formats.name: X vs Y
formats.shape: Two things side by side, one measurable difference, a winner.
formats.example: AI vs VFX: who does it better? / 1080p vs 4K

formats.name: stop doing / myth
formats.shape: 'Stop believing X' or '"X can't happen" - wrong.' then the evidence.

formats.name: peak first
formats.shape: Open on the most dramatic moment, then rewind to explain how it got there.
formats.example: Higgsfield's hook rule: 'start with the peak of the scene'

hooks: State the result in the first 2 seconds, then 'here's how' (Higgsfield: 'Motion design is now easier than ever. What you're seeing was not made by a human.').
A number that sounds impossible, said plainly ('250-ton rockets caught mid-air').
A question the viewer cannot answer yet ('Why can't an ant escape a simple circle?').
Contradict a belief ('You've never actually touched anything').
End with a one-word-answer question to the viewer ('Do you think AI will replace motion designers too?') - it brings comments.
